reproduce.title: Check physical Win-to-Alt shortcut delivery
reproduce.version_requirement: Current PowerToys and supported Windows build
prerequisites: Use an app with Alt+G and Alt+S shortcuts; observe Windows Game Bar hotkeys.
steps: Test physical Left Win+G and Left Win+S with remap enabled; record app and shell behavior.
Repeat reverse Left Alt/Left Win mapping if available; record any extra chord or stuck modifier.
reproduce.expected_result: Physical Left Win maps to the intended application Alt shortcut without unintended shell Win/Alt activation or stuck modifier; record current behavior if not.

judgment.rationale: The original Blender repro and later comments confirm related Win/Alt shortcut interference across apps and current Windows. A plausible hypothesis is that shell-registered Win shortcuts still see the physical source key, but current OS behavior and hook path need reproduction.
evidence: Open Issue-Bug with Needs-Triage, Needs-Team-Response, Product-Keyboard Manager labels; no assignee.
Original report maps Left Win→Left Alt; Blender Alt+G fails or Game Bar responds while Alt+S works; reports PowerToys 0.63 and Blender 3.3.x.
Later comments report Win+R/Win+G interference; August 2025 commenter reports Windows 11 24H2 build 26100.4946 and PowerToys 0.92.1.
Latest comment (2026-03-08) says #43826 may be a duplicate; #43826 is closed but has no public closure rationale, so relation is related, not confirmed duplicate.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce Left Win→Left Alt on current Windows/PowerToys, comparing application Alt shortcuts and shell/Game Bar chord before proposing an input change.

title: Remapping physical [Left Win] -> to [Left Alt] key, cause issues with shortcuts in some app

fix_assessment.rationale: No confirmed fix is linked. Cross-application and shell-hotkey reports support a testable input-delivery hypothesis, but current behavior must be verified.

proposed_fixes.title: Preserve Win-to-Alt remap semantics for system shortcuts
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: the shell still observes physical Left Win while Keyboard Manager exposes remapped Left Alt, producing an unintended Win/Alt chord or consuming the application shortcut. Hook ordering, reserved hotkey behavior, and app-specific handling remain competing explanations.
plan: On current Windows, reproduce Left Win→Left Alt and compare Alt+G/Alt+S in an app with whether Game Bar or another shell hotkey activates.
Trace key-down/up and shell/application-visible modifiers for the failing chord; check OS-reserved hotkeys before changing global remap behavior.
If the source modifier leaks through, normalize it at the remap boundary and cover Win→Alt, reverse mapping, key-up ordering, and unaffected shell shortcuts.
verification: Verify physical Left Win+G acts as Alt+G without unintended shell/Game Bar activation.
Verify Win+E and ordinary Alt chords still work and no modifier sticks after release.

confidence.rationale: Multiple users report related symptoms, but reserved OS shortcuts and app behavior leave the exact failing component uncertain.

issue_context.summary: Remapping physical Left Win to Left Alt breaks selected application shortcuts, and reports suggest the original Win chord may still reach shell hotkeys.
known_information: Open Issue-Bug, Needs-Triage, Needs-Team-Response, Product-Keyboard Manager; no assignee.
Original report says Left Win→Left Alt makes Blender Alt+G fail while Alt+S works; PowerToys 0.63 and Blender 3.3.x.
Later comments describe Game Bar interference, including Windows 11 24H2/PowerToys 0.92.1.

inferences: Physical Win may still be visible to shell-registered shortcuts after remapping, but this is not confirmed.
Reports may share an input boundary issue; reverse mappings and applications differ.
issue_context.analysis: Specific reports justify maintainer-side reproduction rather than generic reporter logs. Keep a yellow hypothesis because shell reservation, hook ordering and application handling remain plausible alternatives.
